claims.source: US Air Force Fact Sheet, Public Affairs Division, Wright-Patterson AFB, January 1985, reproduced by the National Archives
claims.text: The USAF public fact sheet distributed by Wright-Patterson AFB in January 1985 states: 'Periodically, it is erroneously stated that the remains of extraterrestrial visitors are or have been stored at Wright-Patterson AFB. There are not now nor ever have been, any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.'

claims.text: The Wright-Patterson custody terminus is documented by the operating unit, not inferred. The 1127th USAF Field Activities Group's own semiannual history for 1 January to 30 June 1967 records under Project BLUE FLY that its Staff Operations Branch 'coordinated requirements necessary to deploy the FTD exploitation personnel and to airlift personnel and parts from site of acquisition to Wright-Patterson AFB', and that the Joint Chiefs approved F/AD-I priority for short-notice BLUE FLY airlift contingencies.

desc: BLUE FLY was the airlift and quick-reaction arm attached to MOON DUST: the standing arrangement by which recovered material of unknown origin was moved, on priority, to Air Force technical intelligence at Foreign Technology Division, Wright-Patterson AFB. Where MOON DUST was the collection authority, BLUE FLY was the transport and custody mechanism. The two names appear together in Air Force intelligence correspondence and in congressional correspondence generated when members of Congress - including New Mexico's delegation in the 1990s - asked the Air Force to explain them. The Air Force's answers shifted over time from denying the programmes existed to conceding they existed but concerned only foreign space debris. For a board tracking custody, BLUE FLY is the most important single word in the 1960s-1980s record: it names the pipeline. Any recovered material entering US custody in that period had a designated route, and that route terminated at Wright-Patterson, which is precisely where the 1947-era chain also terminated and where the Air Force's own 1985 public fact sheet felt it necessary to state that 'there are not now nor ever have been, any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.'
